label: paragraph_title
text: TUESDAY, APRIL 27, 1926.

label: header
text: THE CHINA MAIL

label: paragraph_title
text: BRITAIN'S BUDGET.

label: text
text: The Government did not intend to renew the Trade Facilities Act, which had exhausted its useful needs.

label: text
text: The estimated revenue on the existing basis of taxation was £804,700,000. Thus, the estimated deficit on the existing basis of taxation would be £7,941,000.

label: text
text: "Mr. Churchill dwell on the happy effects of the restoration and the gold standard, including the normalising of exchanges with the great gold-using Dominions, placing our return to prosperity on a solid basis."

label: text
text: The silk duties had worked with unexpected smoothness. He was convinced that the textile industries in Lancashire which he had been accused of ruining would regard the possibility of a repeal of the silk duties with dismay. There had been recently a check on the consumption of artificial silk, but the trade continued to progress. The foreigner paid Customs duties on artificial silk at present prices rather below last year's, whilst we secured a revenue of between £6,000,000 and £7,000,000 in a full year without making dearer the finery for poor working girls! (Ministerial cheers).

label: text
text: Steps will be taken to prevent a repetition of the heavy losses and dislocation of trade last year due to dumping in the interval between the announcement of the silk tax and the passage of the Budget.

label: paragraph_title
text: Empire Préférence.

label: text
text: Empire preference yielded satisfactory results, notably: wines, tobacco, and rutsins. He proposed to extend the principle for ten years and guarantee all articles at present subject to Imperial preference.

label: text
text: He proposed a betting tax of five per cent. on every stake on the race-course or through a credit bookmaker, and a new import duty of 16.2/3 on wrapping paper. The McKenna duties would be extended to commercial motor cars. He had decided to re-enact for a period of 10 years Part I of the Safeguarding of Industries Act relating to essential factors in national defence, which otherwise would lapse this year.

label: paragraph_title
text: French Finances.

label: text
text: Without prejudice to the impending debt settlement, M. Pèreot had undertaken to pay £4,000,000 in the coming year.

label: text
text: Mr. Churchill, amid cheers, paid a tribute to this proof of French determination and financial power to strengthen the credit of France by a proper regulation of her external debt.

label: text
text: He declared that henceforth one-third of the motor taxes would go to general revenue instead of the special road fund. This, together with the new taxation, would produce £22,000,000 more, which could be devoted to a remission of taxation, but after wiping out the originally, anticipated deficit of £7,941,000, £10,000,000 would be allocated to the sinking fund, which would this year be £60,000,000 compared with £50,000,000 normally remaining for four early marked contingencies, including the cost settlement.

label: text
text: He foreshadowed that in the event of prolonged industrial paralysis he would be compelled to recommend substantial direct and indirect taxation; but apart from unforeseen events, he could see his way fairly clearly to finance the next two years.

label: paragraph_title
text: SPANISH FLIGHT.

label: text
text: SPECIAL ORDER BY THE AIR MINISTRY.

label: text
text: KING ALFONSO'S THANKS.

label: text
text: (British Wireless Service.)

label: text
text: A special Order issued by the Air Ministry states that King Alfonso has telegraphed to King George

label: text
text: My people, the Spanish Army, and myself are sincerely and immensely grateful for splendid and successful search operations in finding in the desert Captain Estevez and his mechanic. Please convey these feelings of gratitude to your brilliant and courageous Air Force for their perilous and noble enterprise. I beg you to allow me to have the pleasure to confer a decoration as a token of recognition and appreciation of my nation to the chiefs and officers who have distinguished themselves in this work of humanity and fellowship. King George had replied expressing his appreciation and assenting gladly to the decoration.

label: paragraph_title
text: RUSSIAN TREATY.

label: text
text: WHAT GERMANY HAS SIGNED IN BERLIN

label: text
text: WAR CONTINGENCIES.

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: Berlin, April 26.

label: text
text: The text of the Russo-German Treaty has been issued and comprises four articles.

label: text
text: It begins by stating that both will do everything toward maintaining peace, and that they are convinced that the interests of the Russian and German peoples necessitate an intimate co-operation.

label: text
text: Firstly,—The basis of relations between the two Governments remains the Treaty of Rapallo, and they will remain in friendly touching in order to reach an understanding on political and economic questions.

label: text
text: Secondly.—Should one of the signatories, in spite of its peaceful attitude, be attacked by a third Power or several Powers, then the other signatory shall remain neutral throughout the entire conflict.

label: text
text: Thirdly.—If a coalition of three Powers is formed with the object of imposing an economic or financial boycott against one of the signatories, the other shall not join the coalition.

label: text
text: Fourthly.—The Treaty will last or five years. Before the expiry of the Treaty both parties will keep each other informed in regard to the further orientation of their political relations.

label: text
text:
In a covering, letter to M. Krestinsky, the Soviet Ambassador, Dr. Stresemann, German Minister for Foreign Affairs, emphasises that Germany's entry into the League of Nations cannot be an obstacle to the development of friendly Russo-German relations.
The German Government is determined to assist in making the idea of peaceful settlement in international disputes a reality, but in the unlikely event of efforts contradicting this basic idea of peace being directed against Russia then Germany will oppose them as strongly as possible.

label: text
text: League Obligations.

label: text
text: The principles of German policy toward the Soviet cannot be influenced by Germany's loyal adherence to the obligations ensuing on her entry into the League concerning Articles XVI. and XVII. of the Covenant of the League on questions of sanctions, which are applicable to Russia only in the event of Russia warning against another country.

label: text
text:
The question as to whether Russia is the attacker can be de-
delded only with Germany's full agreement, so that accusations by other countries shall not be binding for Germany if Germany is not convinced of their justification.

label: paragraph_title
text: WHITE STAR LINE.

label: text
text:
REPORTS OF SALE TO
BRITISH PREMATURE

label: text
text: NEGOTIATIONS IN PROGRESS

label: text
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text:
New York, April 26.
Messrs. Morgan, Grenfell and Company, and Mr. P. A. Franklin, President of the International Mercantile Marine Company, views as "premature" the reports in the Press.

label: text
text: They have authorised an announcement that negotiations are proceeding for the purchase of shares in the White Star Line by a British group represented by Messrs. Morgan, Grenfell and Company. A provisional agreement has been reached, but the numerous details will take time to arrange.

label: text
text: A dennite announcement will be made when a settlement is reached, but in the meanwhile it may be stated that, if the negotiations mature, Messrs. Furness, Withy and Company will be the principal shipping interest in the purchasing syndicate.

label: paragraph_title
text: PEACE PARLEYS

label: text
text: "LATER "NEWS HOPEFUL

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: Ujda, April 26.

label: text
text: The Franco-Spanish Governments have fixed May 1 as the time limit for the conclusion of negotiations with the Riffs. If no agreement is reached, then the Franco-Spanish troops will resume the offensive.

label: text
text:
Udja, April 26.
The French and Spaniards have agreed to, wavel the preliminary conditions of the peace conference.
The Riffs' delegates are expected to return to the conference and proceed on the basis of the original terms.

label: text
text: It was reported on April 19 that the difficulties which have arisen in the Moroccan peace conference, in connection with which one of the Rim delegates has flown in a French aeroplane to consult with Abd-el-Krim and the Chiefs of the Tribes; is explained in a statement by the Riff delegates that they are unable to accept, without modification, the Franco-Spanish demands for the immediate release of prisoners and the unhindered advance of Franco-Spanish troops on certain positions at present occupied by Riffs before the official negotiations have opened.—A Paris cable of April 21 reported: A report from Ujnd states that the Morocco Peace Conference broke up this evening; no decision being reached in regard to the preliminaries for the peace negotiations. The date of the next conference has not been fixed, the delegates wishing to consult their Governments prior to another meeting.

label: paragraph_title
text: WAR DEBTS.

label: text
text: FRENCH OFFER TO UNITED STATES

label: text
text: MUST BE REVISED.

label: text
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text: Washington, April 26.

label: text
text: The Debt Commission has decided that France must revise her debt offer, but emphasised that the latest discussions have not terminated.

label: text
text: The correspondent adds that one of the chief hitches is how much France can pay at the outset.

label: text
text: The Debt Commission is firmly against the “safety clause,” by means of which France would be relieved of her debt responsibilities in the event of Germany's failure to meet her reparations payments.

label: text
text: M. Henri Berenger, the French Ambassador, is not expected to insist on this clause.

label: text
text: M. Peret, Minister for Finance, is expected to go to London next week as the agreement with America will probably be signed in the meantime.

label: text
text: Belgian Agreement.

label: text
text: The Senate has ratified the Belgian debt agreement by 55 votes to 20.

label: paragraph_title
text: RACE TO POLE

label: text
text:
BYRD EXPEDITION IN
NORWAY.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: London, April 26.

label: text
text: The latest move in connection with the race to the Pole is contained in the report from Oslo that the steamer "Chantler" with the Byrd expedition aboard, passed Trondhjem Fjord yesterday, and was met at sea by a Norwegian steamer which transferred to the "Chantler" "certain equipment."

label: doc_title
text: ALLEGED MURDER.

label: text
text:
ORIGINAL TRIAL FULL OF
ERROPS

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text:
Mexico City, April 25.
There was a re-echo of a
celebrated case to-day when the
Supreme Court ordered the re-trial
of Alejo García and Francisco
Ruiz, who were sentenced to death
for the alleged murder of Mrs.
Rosulle Evans, the wife of a British
subject, who was shot dead near
her estate on August 2, 1924.
The Court held that the original
trial was full of errors. The order
automatically stays the death
sentence.
HELD IN CAMERA.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: Paris, April 28

label: text
text:
The trial began to-day of the alleged British spies.
The tribunal decided to proceed with the trial in camera.

label: text
text: A Paris message of March 30 stated:—

label: text
text: The three alleged English spies and two women accomplices have been committed to trial for having collected or attempted to collect information regarding the security and defence of the country.

label: text
text:
A previous Paris cable stated:—
A dramatic turn has developed
in the spy case.

label: paragraph_title
text: Dramatile Turn.

label: text
text: Fischer, one of the three Englishmen who were arrested, who is of Polish extraction, declared that he was convinced that Marthe Moreuil acted as spy on behalf of Leather, another of the arrested Englishmen who repeatedly conversed with her in low tones. Once this happened at Burndetpbleriot's office, with which the three men are connected, after which Leather accompanied Mdle Moreuil to the railway station, giving her instructions for a secret mission to the South of France.

label: text
text: The examining magistrate, M. Peyr, on hearing this, immediately brought Leather and Fischer face to face, when Leather contemptuously stated that the allegations were false.

label: paragraph_title
text: RACIAL FEUDS.

label: text
text: FURTHER VIOLENT CRIMES IN CALCUTTA.

label: text
text: ROUND-UP OF ROUGHS.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Calcutta, April 26.

label: text
text: Hindu were stabbed to death to-day. Two of the men injured yester-day have died.

label: text
text:
A Hindu was killed last night at
Kidderpore.

label: text
text: The majority of the injured men in hospital are Mahommedans. Practically all the shops in the Indian quarters are closed.

label: text
text: There was a general round-up of roughs this morning. When 58 persons, mostly Mahommedans, were arrested in the Kidderpore district.

label: paragraph_title
text: METEORITE FALLS.

label: text
text: The “Kokumin” reports that a meteorite measuring eight by three centimetres and weighing 287 grammes fell at Hongo, a crowded part of Tokyo, on Sunday, sinking two and a half feet into the ground.—Reuter's Pacific Service.

label: text
text: Father L. Robert, Mr. T. C. Monaghan and Mr. Dick Norton were passengers on the s.s. "President Jefferson" which arrived in port yesterday.

label: text
text: Attempting to export $50 by hiding it in his shoe, a Chinese was fined $10 at the Central Magistracy this morning. An-other who had over $2,000 in the same place had to pay $100.

label: paragraph_title
text: ACROSS SIBERIA.

label: text
text: LONDON TO CHINA IN THIRTEEN DAYS

label: text
text: IMPORTANT AGREEMENT

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: The “Morning Post” says that news has been received in London that an agreement has been reached in principle between the Soviet Government and the International Sleeping Car Company for the restoration of the Trans-Siberian express, whereby it will be possible to reach China overland from London in 13 days and Japan in 14 days.

label: text
text: The agreement has not yet been signed, but there is excellent reason to believe that it soon will be.

label: text
text: Plans for the d)lication of the Trans-Siberian part of the line are being considered. The fares will approximate to steamship fares.

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON POLITICS:

label: text
text: DANDIES OF KWANGTUNG

label: text
text: General Wu Te-chen, Commissioner for Police in Canton, has been dismissed.

label: text
text: News of this action by the Kwantung military council reached Hongkong on Sunday, and the matter has now been confirmed by the Canton vernacular papers.

label: text
text: A factor, which led to the report appearing to be strange, was that Mr. Wu was still at liberty in Canton after action had been taken against him.

label: text
text: The only inference is that Mr. Wu's name has been associated, rightly or wrongly, with the Rightist party of the Kuomintang. Most of the senior military officers are described as of the Leftist faction.

label: text
text: Wu still retains command of his division of soldiers who, by their spick and span uniform, have been described as the dandjes of the Kwangtung Army. He had previously tendered his resignation but was pressed to remain in office.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE GLOBE TROTTERS

label: text
text: MISS BETTY NORTON IN NEW NUMBER.

label: text
text: The Globe Trotters, owing to the steamer being delayed a day, will not open their show at the Star Theatre until Friday night next at 9.15.

label: text
text: At the request of Mr. Norton's many friends the Globe Trotters will give a matinee on Sunday afternoon, commencing at 5.30 o'clock.

label: text
text: Mrs. Dick Norton and her daughter Betty will definitely appear in new numbers notwithstanding the many rumours to the contrary, which rumours have caused much surprise to both Mr. and Mrs. Dick, Norton.

label: text
text: A Chinese was taken to the Government Civil Hospital yesterday suffering from injuries to the face and head inflicted with a hammer. He alleges that he was assaulted by some men when he caught them peeping into a bathroom.
